clue.text: Sydney's mate is the last man short leg dropped

indicators.note: dropped says a letter is left out of the shoemaker's word

parts.note: a cobbler is a shoemaker, the man who works on a last, the foot-shaped block
L is the short form of leg, as in cricket's leg side

explanation.surface: A cricket report says the last batsman was dropped by the fielder at short leg.
explanation.walkthrough: The cricket picture of a last man and short leg is false: the last is the cobbler's tool. 'Sydney's mate' points to Australian slang.
explanation.definitionFit: In Australian slang a cobber is a pal or companion, so it is what an Aussie calls a friend.

clue.text: Attentive old boy, the butler?

parts.note: OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil
a butler is a household servant

explanation.surface: An elderly butler is paying close attention.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone observant is watchful and quick to notice things, the sense of attentive.

clue.text: Embargo on witches leaving city in England for an Irish town

parts.note: a ban is an embargo or prohibition

indicators.note: leaving says the coven departs from the city's name

parts.note: Coventry is a city in the English Midlands
a coven is a gathering of witches

explanation.surface: A ban on witches makes them leave an English city for a town in Ireland.
explanation.walkthrough: COVENTRY is a city in central England; take out COVEN and TRY is left.
explanation.definitionFit: Bantry is a town on Bantry Bay in County Cork in the south-west of Ireland.

clue.text: Once more claims right to enter soldiers' property

parts.note: RE stands for the Royal Engineers, British army soldiers

indicators.note: to enter says the letter for right goes inside the property

parts.note: assets are property or possessions

explanation.surface: A claimant again insists on the right to go into some soldiers' property.
explanation.definitionFit: To assert something again is to restate a claim a second time.

clue.text: Extract the P (say) from PLAYFULLY, otherwise drop a Y

indicators.note: otherwise means arranged in some other way, so the following words are reshuffled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: An instruction for editing a word: take the P out of PLAYFULLY, or else remove a Y.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads 'take the p(iss) playfully', a British slang phrase for mocking someone; the capitals and the letter games are a disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: To mock something in fun by imitating it, taking the mickey playfully, is to send it up in a comic imitation.

clue.text: A little pineapple chunk is ample

indicators.note: a little of the fruit's name means just its first letter

parts.note: a lump is a chunk or piece

explanation.surface: A small chunk of pineapple is plenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Plump means full and rounded, generously proportioned, as ample does.

clue.text: Ruddy duck's first past point of no return, we hear

indicators.note: past says the duck's letter comes after the sound
we hear says the word for the point of no return is taken by its sound

parts.note: Caesar crossed the river Rubicon, a step that could not be undone

indicators.note: first means the opening letter of the bird's word

explanation.surface: A ruddy duck, a kind of waterfowl, flies on past the point of no return.
explanation.walkthrough: A ruddy duck is a real bird, which makes 'Ruddy' look like part of a name rather than the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rubicund describes a face that is red and healthy-looking, a reddish complexion.

clue.text: Worshipped female Eurovision winner, current holder

indicators.note: holder says the singer's name holds the letter for current

parts.note: Dana won the Eurovision Song Contest for Ireland in 1970
I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A female singer who won Eurovision is idolised and still holds the title.
explanation.walkthrough: Dana was an Irish singer who won Eurovision with All Kinds of Everything.
explanation.definitionFit: Diana was the Roman goddess of the hunt and the moon, a female deity who was worshipped.

clue.text: With this cry, he'd get Shenandoah rocking!

definitions.text: With this cry, he'd get Shenandoah rocking!

indicators.note: rocking suggests the letters swaying about into a new order

parts.note: the American folk song title supplies the letter pool
the letters of he'd are the extra ones in the pool beyond the answer

explanation.surface: A singer's cry of praise that would set the old song Shenandoah swinging.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer's letters plus HED rearrange to make SHENANDOAH, and the cry itself would get the song going.
explanation.definitionFit: A shout of praise and adoration in worship, the cry someone gives to get a hymn or song going.

clue.text: I steal one posh mobile to put in an "H"

indicators.note: mobile, as moving freely, says the letters shift into another order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A thief confesses to taking an upmarket mobile phone and being sent to hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: An 'H' on a road sign marks a hospital, so to put someone in an 'H' is to admit them there.
explanation.definitionFit: To admit someone to a hospital for treatment is to place them in the building the sign marks.

clue.text: Ahead on rounds, we're in the bar stress-free

parts.note: up means ahead, as a team two goals up is in the lead
beats are rounds, the routes a police officer walks

explanation.surface: Someone winning a boxing match on points relaxes in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: The bar is a bar of music, not a pub, and 'rounds' are a police officer's patrols, not boxing or drinks.
explanation.definitionFit: In music, the unaccented beats in a bar, typically the last one before the downbeat, carry no stress.

clue.text: Don't be at odds of (say) 101 to 1

indicators.note: say tells you to speak the letters out and listen

parts.note: in Roman numerals 101 is CI and 1 is I, so the phrase is written CI TO I

explanation.surface: A betting tip that a horse is a hundred-and-one-to-one outsider.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests betting odds; instead write the numbers as Roman numerals and say C, I, TO, I out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To agree completely with someone is the opposite of disagreeing or being at odds.

clue.text: Kippers with Ragu sauce — dreadfully non-U, this may get an "O"!

indicators.note: dreadfully says the words are mangled into a different order
non-U, the old phrase for lower-class speech, here says a U is left out

explanation.surface: A snob complains that kippers in a pasta sauce is shockingly lower-class food.
explanation.walkthrough: 'non-U' was a 1950s British label for words and habits not used by the upper class; here it means remove a U. The definition is something that makes you gasp 'Oh!'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something unexpected that turns out better than foreseen draws a gasp of astonishment from the person who meets it.

clue.text: Spiritual leader of Austria in 1999

indicators.note: in places the country's letter inside the number's letters

parts.note: IMM is read as Roman numerals for 1000 short of 2000
A is the international vehicle code for Austria

explanation.surface: Someone asks who led the faithful of Austria at the end of the last century.
explanation.walkthrough: IMM is not a correct Roman numeral (1999 is MCMXCIX), and the setter later apologised for it.
explanation.definitionFit: The person who leads prayers in a mosque, or a Muslim religious leader, is a spiritual guide.

clue.text: Ring trendy friend about gear at first

indicators.note: about says the first pieces go round the gear

parts.note: a ring is round, shaped like the letter O
in means trendy or fashionable
an ally is a friend or supporter
rig means gear or equipment

explanation.surface: A request to phone a fashionable pal about some kit, before anything else.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that was so at first was so from the beginning, in its earliest form.

clue.text: Wenger rubbished one centre half's headers in the London area

indicators.note: rubbished, as something trashed, says the name's letters are wrecked into a new order

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: headers means the first letters of the words that follow

explanation.surface: Arsene Wenger, the Arsenal manager, criticises one of his centre halves for his headers in a London match.
explanation.walkthrough: Arsene Wenger managed Arsenal; a centre half is a central defender in football. 'rubbished' turns WENGER into GREENW.
explanation.definitionFit: Greenwich is a borough of south-east London on the Thames, home of the meridian.

clue.text: U-tube Carl fixed in study by lamplight

indicators.note: fixed, as in rigged or set up, says the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Carl repairs a U-shaped pipe while studying.
explanation.definitionFit: To lucubrate is to work or study laboriously, especially late at night by artificial light.

clue.text: Canteen recipe's peculiar charm

indicators.note: peculiar, meaning odd, says the letters are put in an odd order

parts.note: R is the abbreviation for recipe, Latin for take, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: A canteen's recipe has an odd appeal.
explanation.definitionFit: To entrance someone is to enchant or delight them, filling them with wonder.

clue.text: Left wondering as to number one Guardian setter

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one
Shed is a pseudonym of a Guardian crossword setter

explanation.surface: Someone is baffled about which Guardian crossword setter is the best.
explanation.definitionFit: To be left amazed and unable to explain something is to be greatly surprised.

clue.text: Small, docked tail

parts.note: S is the usual abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels
docked means cut short, as with an animal's tail

explanation.surface: A small animal has had its tail docked.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Take C from ICE (say), a cube thrown heartlessly at soft drink

indicators.note: heartlessly means the middle letter of the cube's word is removed

parts.note: a die is a cube thrown in games
Coke is a brand of soft drink

explanation.surface: A recipe for a drink: take ice, throw in a cube, and add a soft drink.
explanation.walkthrough: ICE stands for internal combustion engine, and C is the symbol for carbon, so the definition means remove carbon deposits from an engine.
explanation.definitionFit: To decoke an engine is to clean out the carbon deposits that build up inside it.

clue.text: Basically the same thing, beer and ale — can get drunk!

indicators.note: get drunk says the letters stagger about into a new order

explanation.surface: A drinker reckons beer and ale are much the same, as long as you can get drunk on them.
explanation.walkthrough: The fodder is THING, BEER, ALE and CAN, which rearrange to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Things that can be swapped for one another without difference are in effect identical.

clue.text: Add to RAM

parts.note: a tup is a ram, a male sheep, in northern English dialect

explanation.surface: An instruction to increase a computer's memory.
explanation.walkthrough: RAM looks like computer memory, but it is the male sheep, a tup.
explanation.definitionFit: To tot up figures is to add them together to get a total.

clue.text: Rubbish collected from Ohio hotel regularly at day's end

indicators.note: regularly means every other letter is taken from the words that follow
end means the last letter of the word before it

explanation.surface: Trash is picked up from an Ohio hotel every evening.
explanation.definitionFit: Hooey is informal American slang for nonsense, worthless talk.

clue.text: Use a bit of what's essential to recreate a Tintoretto

indicators.note: essential to says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: An art copyist uses up part of their stock of paint to reproduce a Venetian master's picture.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft definition took in 'what's', but that word is only a link to the wordplay; 'Use a bit of' alone swaps for the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: To consume part of a resource, as savings or time, is to wear it down by using some.

clue.text: A region cultivated many years earlier

indicators.note: cultivated, as ground is worked over, says the letters are turned into a new order

explanation.surface: A stretch of land was farmed long ago.
explanation.definitionFit: The prehistoric period when iron tools came into use was a long era in the distant past.

clue.text: Fast Scottish river turned into another that's not English

indicators.note: into says the turned river goes inside the other one
not says the following letter is removed

parts.note: the Spey is another Scottish river

indicators.note: turned says the river's name is read backwards

parts.note: the Dee is a river in Aberdeenshire, Scotland

explanation.surface: A fast Scottish river is diverted into another one that is not in England.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned' gives EED, the Dee backwards; it goes into SPY, the Spey without its E, signalled by 'not' and 'English'.
explanation.definitionFit: Something speedy moves quickly, the plain sense of fast.

clue.text: Listed what the last man at the top did?

definitions.meaning: listed means leaned over to one side, as a ship does

definitions.text: what the last man at the top did?
definitions.meaning: the last man of the top clue, 1 across, is a cobbler, who fits new heels to shoes

explanation.walkthrough: 'the last man at the top' refers back to 1 across, the top of the grid, where the last man is a cobbler.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship that heeled over tipped to one side; a cobbler who heeled a shoe gave it a new heel.
